chunks: From him, from Hanaan, who said:

I was sitting with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). Muammar al-Zayyat said to him: 'We buy oil in its containers, and a deficiency is calculated for us in it due to the nature of the containers.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'If it increases and decreases, there is no harm; but if it increases and does not decrease, do not approach it.'

key_terms.أَزْقَاقِهِ: its containers (plural of ziqq, a type of oil skin or jar)
key_terms.لِمَكَانِ ٱلْأَزْقَاقِ: due to the nature/condition of the containers
key_terms.يَزِيدُ وَ لاَ يَنْقُصُ: it increases and does not decrease (fixed/increasing only)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying oil in containers where a fixed amount is deducted for the container's weight or volume?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the application of *gharar* (uncertainty) in commercial transactions involving bulk goods like oil, where measurement discrepancies are inherent. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between acceptable, fluctuating measurement variances (*ziyadah wa nuqsan*) and unacceptable, fixed deficiencies that effectively constitute a hidden defect or deception, thereby protecting the buyer from unjust loss. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on transparency and fairness, ensuring that minor, unavoidable trade imperfections do not invalidate the contract.
